prerequisites: Minimum prior knowledge, skills, and attitudes are required. Knowledge corresponds, in part, to what is required in previous education programs. It is important for students to have or quickly acquire knowledge of the dihedric system applied to industrial drawing (projections and their orientations), types of lines and their use, formats, etc.
No prior experience with CAD software is required, but it is beneficial if students have had the opportunity to use some previously.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire a study/work methodology and be able to deepen independently in the knowledge area of Graphic Expression to propose and solve the graphic problems encountered in professional life.
Use Technical Drawing as a communication language, both in terms of work methodologies and tools used.
Apply the concept of Standardization: presentation formats, scales, symbology, etc., in graphical representations.
Solve geometric problems and their application in the construction of industrial parts.
Represent industrial parts by means of dimensioned sketches, applying existing regulations and criteria.
Interpret technical drawings and assembly plans, distinguishing between the functions of each element.
Represent certain elements commonly used in industry, know their designation and standardization.
Consult regulations, analyzing and structuring information.
Analyze and compare the characteristics and applications of the most used CAD programs in Engineering.

Know and manage a CAD program, making use of all its possibilities for defining entities, geometric transformations and drawing aids, dimensioning, etc., transferring previously acquired concepts and skills.
Manage a project-based CAD system.
Locate, analyze, and structure necessary information for projects.
Integrate drawings with other applications to generate technical documentation in a comprehensive and organized manner.
Work in a team, assuming responsibility and collaborating with colleagues.
Plan activities to deliver work within assigned times and with required quality.
Participate in class, respectfully and argue with rational criteria.
Use the appropriate type of Industrial Drawing to graphically represent industrial elements.
Practice sketching, in which you must: Represent objects using lines, differentiating their function. Label drawings clearly and carefully.
Use standardization in your drawings and plans: Formats and title blocks, lines, lettering.
Represent the position and relationship of graphic elements in dihedral space.
Identify and represent standardized Orthogonal Views of industrial objects.
Use CAD tools to create drawings and plans.
Dimension industrial elements and spaces according to standards.
Use Cuts and sections to clarify the graphical representation of parts.
Represent industrial elements and spaces in isometric perspective.
Develop professional texts or scientific-technical reports according to the conventions of the discipline.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Introduction. Fundamentals of projections. Geometric drawing. Representation techniques.
Topic 2. Industrial Drawing. Tracing and interpretation of dihedral views. Sketching.
Topic 3. Sketching. Computer-aided applications (CAD): Fundamentals of freehand sketching and introduction to Autocad.
Topic 4. Standardization: technical drawing standards and industrial standardization. Concept. Formats and folding of plans. Title block. Types of lines. Lettering. Scales.
Topic 5. Main representation systems used in engineering: Dihedral System. Axonometric System.
Topic 9. Construction drawing. Schematic and symbolic representation of electromechanical elements.
teaching_methods: Viewing videos and content prepared by the teacher
Problem-solving exercises in the computer lab
Activities carried out in spaces with specialized equipment (Laboratory/Computer practice)
Research sessions on classroom didactics (Laboratory/Computer practice)
Project work to solve a problem or address a task through planning, design, and execution of activities (Teamwork/Integrated Project)
Study/preparation of readings, exams, exercises, classes (Individual work)
Preparation (individual and group) of essays, problem-solving, projects for submission and presentation (Group work)
assessment_rules: Continuous and personalized assessment is applied. In written tests, a score equal to or greater than 4 is required for the grade to be averaged. Students have two annual calls to pass written tests. Academic assignments submitted late will have points deducted, up to a maximum of 5 points for the exercise; after one week of delay, the exercise will receive a 0. Tasks with a grade below 5 can be resubmitted within one week for a maximum grade of 5. Students can recover the grade for academic assignments in the second call by completing alternative exercises. To pass the subject in both first and second calls, an average grade equal to or greater than 5 is required. Students may waive the Integrated Project grade or continuous assessment in the second call if they notify in writing. AI usage rules are specified: Level 1 (not allowed for exams), Level 2 (allowed with simple citation for support), Level 3 (intensive use allowed with full traceability/prompt history).
